title: [23/11/2023] Daily Internet usage among adults in the UK
prompt: The chart below shows the percentage of adults of different age groups in the UK who used the Internet every day from 2003–2006. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart illustrates the percentage of adults in different age ranges who used the Internet over a four-year period from 2003 to 2006.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, Internet usage increased across all age groups throughout the given period. Notably, the youngest demographic (16-24 years) consistently maintained the highest rates of Internet use, while the eldest group (65 and over) recorded significantly lower percentages throughout the period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Examining the three younger age brackets first, in 2003, approximately 80% of individuals aged 16-24 were Internet users, which was higher than both the 25-44 and 45-54 age groups, at around 50% and 60% respectively. The youngest cohort saw their figures rise to nearly 100% in 2005, though this decreased slightly to about 90% by 2006. In contrast, both the 25-44 and 45-54 age brackets exhibited steady upward trends, with both groups reaching approximately 80% usage by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With respect to the older demographics, Internet usage among the 55-64 group stood at approximately 30% in 2003, while the eldest group (65+) had zero internet usage. The 55-64 bracket subsequently experienced significant growth to around 50% by the end of the period, whereas Internet usage among seniors remained relatively low, reaching just 20% in 2006.
